title: How should dungarees and workwear vests fit during a shift?
description: Specify pockets, strap adjustment, closures and logo placement for ordinary branded workwear. A wearer trial shows what a flat drawing can miss.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: For dungarees and vests, the first fitting should include the objects and layers people carry at work. A pocket can look generously sized on a drawing while its opening is too narrow for a notebook. A vest can fit over a tee and feel restrictive over the sweatshirt staff wear for most of the year.

Write the pilot outcome into the repeat specification

bodyHtml:
Start with what goes in the pockets

For a shop-floor team, collect the notebook, measuring tape or handheld scanner used during a normal shift. Record dimensions and how staff reach for it. Draw the pocket mouth as well as the pocket bag. Test whether the object can be removed one-handed and whether it presses into the body when the wearer sits.

FeatureTest on the wearerNote to return to the maker
Dungaree bibBend, sit and reach up wearing the normal underlayer.Where the top edge sits and whether strap adjustment remains available.
Thigh pocketInsert the real item and walk.Any swinging, pressure or obstruction at the opening.
Vest armholeReach across the body with the intended layer underneath.Where the armhole pulls, gaps or rubs.
Front fasteningOpen and close it during the normal task.Whether the closure can be operated comfortably.

Keep identification visible

A chest logo that works on a flat vest may be partly hidden by a folded edge, strap or removable badge. Mark its position on a worn sample with the vest open and closed. On dungarees, check that the bib pocket and any branding can coexist without the stitches closing part of the pocket.

Test a useful spread of sizes

Choose wearers with different torso lengths and layering needs, and record the garment size tested. A strap that reaches the end of its adjustment on the first wearer leaves little room for a different body shape. Ask the manufacturer which dimensions change across the range and which pocket details remain at a fixed size.

How can you check whether a tool pocket is usable?

Bring the object carried on the job to the fitting. Have the wearer put it in, sit down and remove it with the hand they normally use. Record the point at which it catches and whether the loaded pocket pulls the garment sideways. The intended use gives the pattern maker more direction than a request for a larger pocket.

Write the pilot outcome into the repeat specification

If the trial changes the pocket opening, update both drawing and measurement. Keep a photo of the final item in use, the approved trim reference and the care method used in the trial. For any protective application, have the responsible team specify the required product classification and documentation separately. EU information on PPE at work

Send BEWE4R your vest or dungaree brief along with the job description and the items your employees need to carry.
